items.title: Takiyuddin refuses to withdraw 'munafik' remark, proposes mediation
items.summary: KOTA BARU: Pas secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan has written to the Dewan Rakyat speaker proposing mediation to resolve the controversy over his use of the word "munafik" (hypocrite) in Parliament. Instead, I wrote to the speaker proposing that he convene a mediation session. Takiyuddin said the speaker's office had received the letter on Thursday.

items.title: ‘What you order is what you get’: Zahid says Ab Rauf to return as CM if BN wins Melaka polls
items.summary: JASIN, Oct 23 — Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh will remain Melaka chief minister should Barisan Nasional (BN) and its strategic partners win the state election next month, said Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi. “Insya-Allah, with Datuk Rauf (Ab Rauf), what you ‘order’ is exactly what Melaka will get,” he said when launching the BN election machinery for the Jasin parliamentary constituency at Dewan Alamanda here last night. The Election Commission (EC) has set Nov 14 as polling day for the Melaka State Election, with nomination day on Oct 31 and early voting on Nov 10.

items.title: Selangor Sultan: Monarchy remains a pillar of stability
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Although society has evolved, the fundamental role of a constitutional monarch remains unchanged, the Sultan of Selangor, Sultan Sharafuddin Idris Shah, said. Sultan Sharafuddin said the Constitution provided clear guidance on his responsibilities. The monarchy, he said, represented continuity, stability, service and responsibility.

items.title: PM tells Cabinet to pursue major policy shifts for a more resilient Malaysia
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 24 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has highlighted the need for Cabinet members to look at major policy shifts required to strengthen national resilience in industry and the economy. Anwar said he remained optimistic that Malaysia could forge ahead as a great nation through continued efforts by the Ministry of Investment, Trade and Industry (MITI) and collaboration with industry. Also present were Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani and Deputy Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Sim Tze Tzin.

items.title: Selangor's strength lies in its people, says Sultan
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Sultan of Selangor has credited the people of the state for making his 25 years as ruler a successful and meaningful journey. His Royal Highness Sultan Sharafuddin Idris Shah said Selangor had remained one of the country's most important states, thanks to the contributions of its people and those who had made it their home. Sultan Sharafuddin said preserving harmony among Selangor's diverse communities was equally important.

items.title: Seremban records highest API reading at 169
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Seremban recorded the country's highest Air Pollutant Index (API) reading at 169 as of 8am today, with unhealthy air quality also recorded in several other areas. Bandaraya Melaka recorded an API reading of 163, while Batu Muda in Kuala Lumpur and Bukit Rambai in Melaka registered 162 each. The Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) also reported moderate air quality at 41 monitoring stations nationwide.

items.title: Anwar urges Malaysian industry to modernise and compete globally
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 24 — Budget 2027 provides a comprehensive framework to empower young people by expanding access to quality job opportunities, industry-driven skills training and stronger social protection. Perdana Fellows Alumni Association secretary-general Amir Izzwan Abu Hasan said the budget initiatives covered various key stages of youth development, helping young people build resilience in the face of current economic challenges. “These funds and facilities provide an excellent platform for young people to upskill and reskill, ensuring their skills meet current industry demands.

items.title: Selangor Sultan urges youths to stay united and informed
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Sultan of Selangor hopes future generations of Selangorians will be knowledgeable, compassionate, resilient, united and respectful of others. His Royal Highness Sultan Sharafuddin Idris Shah said young people should strive for excellence without losing their sense of responsibility towards society. Sultan Sharafuddin said the younger generation had rightly placed importance on environmental sustainability and heritage preservation.

items.title: Alumni group: Young Malaysians must seize Budget 2027 career, upskilling opportunities
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 24 — Budget 2027 provides a comprehensive framework to empower young people by expanding access to quality job opportunities, industry-driven skills training and stronger social protection. Perdana Fellows Alumni Association secretary-general Amir Izzwan Abu Hasan said the budget initiatives covered various key stages of youth development, helping young people build resilience in the face of current economic challenges. “These funds and facilities provide an excellent platform for young people to upskill and reskill, ensuring their skills meet current industry demands.

items.title: PN-BN seat allocation for Melaka polls based on incumbency
items.summary: KOTA BARU: The seat allocation between Perikatan Nasional (PN) and Barisan Nasional (BN) for the Melaka state election will be based on the incumbent concept. PN secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan said the concept had been generally agreed upon by all component parties in the coalition. He said Umno was also the incumbent in 21 seats in Melaka.

items.title: #NSTviral: 'Honk twice to congratulate me': First-car celebration goes viral
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A cheeky note on a man's first car turned an ordinary drive in Segamat, Johor, into a moment of celebration when a truck driver behind him honked twice to congratulate him. "I bought a new car. In the comments, the user revealed that the car belonged to a colleague whose first vehicle purchase had prompted an office-wide celebration.

items.title: Police rescue month-old infant dumped under stairs in Kepong’s Desa Aman Puri
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 24 — A baby boy, believed to be about a month old, was found alive in a box under the staircase of an apartment block in Kepong Thursday. Gombak Police chief ACP Ibrahim Husin said police received a report about the discovery from a man in his mid-30s at 9.14 am. He said the baby was believed to have been abandoned by an unidentified individual under the staircase of Block 1, Desa Satu, Desa Aman Puri Apartment, Jalan Puri Kepong.

items.title: Teen dies, five injured as car crashes into tree
items.summary: "The victims comprised two adult men, two adult women and two boys. One of the victims, identified as Putera Muhaimin Qudrat Mohd Noor Wandi, 16, was pronounced dead at the scene. "The five other victims, Puteri Nur Fairuza Balqis Mohd Noor Wandi, 15; Nor Azlan Shaharudin, 27; Putera Khairunas Mohd Noor Wandi, 11; Putera Aidin Firdaus Mohd Noor Wandi, three; and Rahmah A Rahim, 26; were injured and taken to hospital for treatment," he said in a statement today.

items.title: Malaysia-origin vessel seized in Indonesia with 1.16 tonnes of ketamine
items.summary: JAKARTA: Indonesian authorities seized 1.16 tonnes of ketamine from a Mongolian-flagged vessel that had sailed from Malaysia in the waters off North Sumatra province earlier this week, national police chief Suyudi Ario Seto said on Friday. Indonesian authorities, including the police and customs office, intercepted the tanker in the waters off Tanjung Balai in the province earlier this week, Seto said. The ketamine was found in 58 sacks weighing a total of 1.16 tonnes, Seto said.

items.title: Recalculating… TuJu app promises to find its way back by Nov 6
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 24 — The technical team of the TuJu Highway Navigation Application is currently carrying out recovery and improvement work, targeted to be completed by Nov 6 at the latest. The TuJu management, in a statement, said that updates on the recovery work will be communicated through TuJu’s official channels, while other functions in the application can continue to be used as usual for now. In this regard, TuJu apologises to users who have experienced disruptions in navigation functions over the past few days.

items.title: Pentagon designates Confucius Institutes in US a national security threat
items.summary: WASHINGTON: The US Defence Department has designated Chinese-funded cultural centres on university campuses known as Confucius Institutes as a threat to US national security, Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth said on Friday. Washington has long accused Confucius Institutes of being Chinese propaganda tools and has taken steps to crack down on them. Hegseth, in a video posted on social media, alleged that Confucius Institutes were operating under disguise at US universities and that the Pentagon had added them to its list of institutions that threaten US national security.

items.title: Argentine judge dismisses case against Milei over alleged crypto scam
items.summary: BUENOS AIRES: A federal judge on Friday dismissed a criminal case against Argentine President Javier Milei and his sister, in which they were accused of promoting a suspected cryptocurrency scam that resulted in at least US$100 million in losses for investors. $LIBRA." Milei later denied promoting the virtual currency, saying he "did not know the details of the project".

items.title: North Korea's Kim calls for 'military revolution' as he urges stronger army units
items.summary: SEOUL: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un called for the country's army companies to be turned into elite, self-sufficient combat units during a two-day meeting of company commanders in Pyongyang, state media KCNA said on Saturday. The event underscored Kim's consistent policy priority of strengthening the military. In a speech at a conference of company commanders for North Korea's army on Oct 22-23, which KCNA said was the first military-wide gathering since the Ninth Congress of North Korea's ruling party in February, Kim called for every company to be fully prepared so that "the goal of the new-era military build-up" could be achieved.

items.title: Death in custody: No internal injuries found in post-mortem, 78 quizzed
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A post-mortem on a 42-year-old man who died in police custody found no internal organ injuries, although several external injuries were detected. Bukit Aman Integrity and Standards Compliance Department director Datuk Aida Abdul Hamid said the cause of death remained pending laboratory analysis . Aida said the case had been classified as sudden death, with the Death in Custody Criminal Investigation Unit continuing investigations from various angles.

items.title: Melaka polls: PH faces uphill battle, but surprise remains possible [WATCH]
items.summary: But political analysts said DAP and PH could still pull off a surprise by winning over young and undecided voters, particularly in mixed constituencies and seats won with narrow margins. He said support among Chinese and Indian voters, as well as middle-class Malays in urban and semi-urban areas, would be crucial to PH's electoral performance. He said these issues could influence young and undecided voters, potentially benefiting PH if they shift support to the coalition.

items.title: Judge puts off decision on Charlie Kirk murder trial date
items.summary: NEW MEXICO: A Utah judge on Friday said he needed more time to decide when to start the trial of Tyler Robinson, the man accused of killing prominent right-wing activist Charlie Kirk more than a year ago, media reported. At a hearing in Provo, Utah, District Court Judge Tony Graf heard arguments from defence lawyers, prosecutors and a lawyer for Kirk's widow, Erika Kirk, before saying he needed to consider their positions. Robinson's lawyers expect a six-to-seven-month trial.

items.title: Civil servants want clarity over Waze ban
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Civil servants are seeking clarity over the decision to ban them from using the Waze navigation application. "Ordinary Malaysians are also using Waze and their location data could be exposed, too. Waze is banned.

items.title: NST COURT WATCH: Shuhaily charged, Teresa Kok wins suit, Jovian loses appeal & Papagomo acquitted [WATCH]
items.summary: MCBA chief and former Temerloh police chief charged in separate cases KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia Border Control and Protection Agency director-general Datuk Seri Mohd Shuhaily Mohd Zain made headlines after becoming the first high-ranking officer of the agency to be charged with assaulting two Special Branch policemen. He is set to return to court for case management on Nov 25. Below are the other major court cases this week FORMER TEMERLOH POLICE CHIEF JAILED FOR BRIBERY On Wednesday, former Temerloh police chief Superintendent Mohd Azhar Mohd Yusoff was sentenced to eight months in jail after being found guilty of 46 counts of accepting bribes totalling RM69,600 between 2019 and 2023.

items.title: NST CRIME WATCH: Murder, school attack and baby's death dominate the week [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Murder, violence, organised crime and shocking attacks dominated Malaysia's crime headlines this week, with several cases drawing widespread public attention and raising concerns over safety and security. From the murder of a Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (MCBA) officer at a government residential complex in Nilai to an alleged attack on a teacher by a Form Four student at an international school in Kuching, the cases highlighted the range and severity of crimes being investigated by police. Police have recorded statements from 18 people to assist investigations.

items.title: Experts say all high-risk groups vulnerable to haze, including those with medical conditions
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 24 — While haze exposure poses health risks to the general population, high-risk groups such as children, older adults and pregnant women are more vulnerable to its effects. Those with chronic lung diseases and other medical conditions are also among those who need to take precautions against haze exposure. He told Malay Mail that young children with asthma, older adults with heart or lung diseases, and pregnant women with underlying medical conditions may be especially susceptible during haze episodes.

items.title: Haze can irritate skin and eyes, not just lungs, experts warn
items.summary: While haze is commonly associated with respiratory and cardiovascular problems, medical experts say it can also affect the skin and eyes. How haze affects skin and eyes Medical specialist Dr Norafiza Mohd Yasin said PM2.5 particles, which measure 2.5 microns in diameter, can penetrate deep into the lungs and enter the bloodstream, as well as disrupt the skin’s natural barrier. Dr Bala Murali Sundram, a public health medicine specialist at Universiti Malaya’s Faculty of Medicine, said pollutants deposited on exposed skin can contribute to oxidative stress, inflammation and damage to the skin barrier.

items.title: Rubio calls for Cubans to work with CIA, but warns: Be 'discreet'
items.summary: WASHINGTON: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio on Friday urged Cubans to make "discreet" contact with American intelligence services as Washington seeks to force an end to the island's communist government. For months, President Donald Trump and other senior US officials have openly hinted at a military intervention or takeover of Cuba, ramping up economic, political and legal pressure on the country. "Those beautiful (military) ships will pass Cuba.

items.title: Trump ends tariffs on some Canadian products, aiming to help Senator Collins
items.summary: WASHINGTON: With an incumbent Maine US senator from his own party locked in a tight re-election battle, President Donald Trump signed an order on Friday to remove 50 per cent tariffs on some Canadian agricultural and forestry products in a move that could benefit companies in the state. The Republican president's hefty tariffs on Canada have caused friction with the US neighbour to the north while creating problems for American businesses in Maine and other states that rely on certain Canadian goods. With the Nov 3 US midterm elections looming and Republicans fighting to retain control of Congress, Senator Susan Collins had urged the White House to address tariffs on products affecting Maine companies and farmers.

items.title: Protests expected in Rome, Milan under heavy security
items.summary: ROME: Security forces are deploying in large numbers across Italy on Saturday for protests planned in eight cities, including Rome and Milan, after some demonstrations turned violent last weekend. In Milan, extra soldiers deployed following last weekend's protests will patrol the city centre, but Mayor Giuseppe Sala said there were no plans to shut down the city. "Last weekend there weren't enough of us.

items.title: Trump orders lawsuit to block Alaska Senate result if Republicans lose
items.summary: WASHINGTON: President Donald Trump said on Friday that he had ordered a Justice Department lawsuit seeking to prevent certification of Alaska's Senate election result if the Republican incumbent loses — raising further questions over whether he will accept defeat in the midterms. Trump — who tried to overturn the 2020 presidential election after losing to Democrat Joe Biden — has repeatedly questioned the validity of the upcoming election, in which Democrats are forecast to make big gains. Democrats and Sullivan Jr. himself, a registered Republican, have denied this.

items.title: Ebola vaccine trial begins in DR Congo
items.summary: GENEVA: The first clinical trial of an Ebola vaccine during the outbreak gripping the Democratic Republic of Congo began on Friday, the head of the World Health Organisation said. Today, in Bunia DRC, the first participants were vaccinated in a new Ebola vaccine trial called Tumaini, which means 'hope' in Swahili," WHO chief Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus said on X. "This trial will help us understand whether any of the vaccine candidates designed for Bundibugyo virus work.

items.title: Singapore widens haze probe to local firms linked to Indonesian fires
items.summary: SINGAPORE: Singapore expanded on Friday its probe into companies linked to fires in Indonesia, asking 10 locally-based firms for information about their efforts to contain blazes blamed for toxic haze covering the region. Over the past week, Singapore issued notices to 10 foreign-based companies, insisting that they deploy fire fighting teams, stop burning or starting new fires in Indonesia and submit information about their links with associated companies in Indonesia and Singapore. The information is to be reviewed by Singapore's National Environmental Agency (NEA).

items.title: Taiwan warns of 'destructive winds' as Typhoon Champi batters island
items.summary: TAIPEI: A powerful typhoon pounded Taiwan on Friday as authorities warned of "destructive winds" and urged locals to shelter from the storm. Typhoon Champi dumped heavy rain, toppled trees and knocked out power to thousands of households as it swept past Taiwan's northeast on the way to China and Japan. One person has been killed in Taiwan after being swept away by waves whipped up by the typhoon, authorities said.

items.title: Casualties feared as multi-storey building collapses in Nairobi
items.summary: NAIROBI: A multi-storey building collapsed mid-construction in the Kenyan capital on Friday, with many feared trapped in the rubble and accusations of dangerous building work. The building was reduced to a pile of rubble as search and rescue teams arrived on the scene, but struggled to start accessing the site which was jammed between other high-rise buildings. Kenya's National Building Inspectorate report found that 87 per cent of buildings audited nationwide last year failed to meet standards or lacked the required approvals.

items.title: PN ready to use Pas logo if barred from using own in Melaka polls
items.summary: KOTA BARU: Perikatan Nasional (PN) is prepared to contest the Nov 14 Melaka election using the Pas logo if it cannot use its own. PN election director Datuk Seri Muhammad Sanusi Md Nor said the coalition had no objection to contesting under either the PN logo or Pas' moon symbol. If we cannot use the PN logo, we will use the Pas logo.

items.title: Rauf to remain Melaka CM if BN wins state polls, says Zahid
items.summary: JASIN: Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh will remain Melaka Chief Minister should Barisan Nasional and its strategic partners win the state election next month, said Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi. "With Datuk Rauf, what you 'order' is exactly what Melaka will get," he said when launching the BN election machinery for the Jasin parliamentary constituency at Dewan Alamanda/ The Election Commission has set Nov 14 as polling day for the Melaka election, with nomination day on Oct 31 and early voting on Nov 10. BN won 21 of the 28 seats contested in the 2021 Melaka state polls, paving the way for the coalition to form the state government, while Pakatan Harapan secured five seats and Perikatan Nasional two.

items.title: Birthday plans cut short after boy, 7, falls to his death from PPR block
items.summary: His mother, Norhidayah Yacob, 30, said the family had planned to celebrate Mohammad Adib Rizqy Mohammad Fauzi's birthday yesterday but had to postpone it because her husband, Mohammad Fauzi Zurin, 31, who works as a lorry attendant, had yet to receive his salary. "We had planned to celebrate my son's birthday next Tuesday, as it is also my husband's birthday. My son also passed away on this blessed Friday," she said when met at the scene.

items.title: Nga: Future cities must balance modern technology with heritage preservation
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: Future urban development must balance technological advancement with the preservation of national heritage and identity to create comfortable, sustainable and climate-resilient cities. Housing and Local Government Minister Nga Kor Ming said traditional design principles could be combined with modern technology to build homes better suited to local conditions, including hot weather and flood risks. Nga, who is also president of the UN-Habitat Assembly, cited traditional Malay houses as an example of architecture that could inspire modern housing development.

items.title: MCMC investigates Facebook’s failure to block livestream of teacher attack in Kuching, says Fahmi
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 23 — The Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) is investigating Facebook’s failure to detect or block a livestream of an attack on a teacher in Kuching, said Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil. The Madani government spokesperson said he would leave it to MCMC to investigate the incident before making any further comments. “MCMC is currently investigating the matter.

items.title: Fahmi tells LLM, Prosignal to explain TuJu app glitches and fixes
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 23 — The Malaysian Highway Authority (LLM) and Prosignal Consortium Sdn Bhd have been asked to provide a detailed explanation of problems affecting users of the local navigation app TuJu, including their causes, technical issues and corrective measures. “The explanation from LLM and Prosignal is crucial to addressing users' concerns comprehensively, improving TuJu's reliability and strengthening public confidence in the local navigation app,” he told a post-Cabinet meeting press conference here today. Last Tuesday, the government encouraged Malaysians to use TuJu, developed by LLM, as an alternative navigation app.

items.title: Anwar apologises over Waze ban linked to Israel, says national security comes first (VIDEO)
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 23 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has apologised if the decision to ban a navigation application owned by an entity linked to the Israeli regime causes any inconvenience to the public. “I apologise if the decision to ban this navigation application, which belongs to the Israeli regime, causes inconvenience to the public. Last Wednesday, the government decided to prohibit all civil servants from using the navigation application Waze, in order to safeguard government information and users' personal data against the threat of misuse by the Israeli regime.

items.title: Abang Johari: Some GPS incumbents willing to make way for new faces in Sarawak polls
items.summary: KUCHING, Oct 23 — Some incumbent Gabungan Parti Sarawak (GPS) assemblymen have indicated they are willing to make way for new candidates in the coming state election, said Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Openg. He said the coalition’s line-up would comprise a mix of experienced and younger leaders, with new faces expected to feature. Earlier, Abang Johari announced that the Sarawak Legislative Assembly (DUN) would be dissolved on October 26 to pave the way for the next state election.

items.title: Female tapir killed in suspected collision on LPT2 near Kijal
items.summary: Terengganu Department of Wildlife and National Parks (Perhilitan) director Dennis Ten Choon Yung said the department received information about the incident from the LPT2 management at 8am before four officers from the Kemaman district office were dispatched to the scene an hour later to investigate and conduct an inspection. He said the inspection found that the 200-kilogramme tapir suffered head injuries, several abrasions on its body and a fractured left hind leg, believed to have been caused by the collision. Dennis said the Bukit Kambing Forest Reserve was the nearest forest reserve to the scene, located about seven kilometres from where the tapir was found.

items.title: Federal Court to hear Negeri Sembilan exco members’ dismissal challenge on Dec 16
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 23 — The Federal Court has set December 16 to hear the legal bid filed by ten deposed Negeri Sembilan State Executive Council (Exco) members to challenge the state ruler’s decision last month to revoke their appointments. The 10 are Datuk Mohd Faizal Ramli, Datuk Zaifulbahri Idris, Mustapha Nagoor, Siow Kong Choon, Siti Nur Umaira Hasim, Datuk Mohd Asna Amin, Datuk Mohd Razi Mohd Ali, Suhaimizan Bizar, Datuk Mohd Fairuz Mohd Isa and Datuk Razali Abu Samah. They filed the notice of motion on October 14 and named the Negeri Sembilan State Secretary and the State Government as respondents.

items.title: ‘Completely false’: Waze rejects Malaysia’s data security claims after civil servant ban
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 23 — Navigation app Waze rejected on Friday Malaysia’s allegations that it could exploit users’ personal data, after the country banned civil servants from using the app over its Israeli links. Malaysian Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim announced the ban on Wednesday to “safeguard government information and users’ personal data against the threat of misuse by the Israeli regime”. “Claims that Waze collects sensitive government information or allows any entity to exploit personal user data are completely false,” a Waze spokesperson told AFP in a statement.

items.title: Ready for floods and extreme heat? North-east monsoon begins Oct 27, MetMalaysia warns
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 23 — The 2026/2027 North-east Monsoon (MTL) is expected to begin on October 27 and continue until March next year, according to Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) director-general Dr Mohd Hisham Mohd Anip. “Continuous strong north-easterly winds could also cause rough seas and rising sea levels in the South China Sea,” he said in a media statement today. As the monsoon enters its final phase, from January to March 2027, Mohd Hisham said rainfall was expected to decrease, particularly in the northern states of Peninsular Malaysia and Sabah.

items.title: Queen concerned over worsening mental health issues among children, teens
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 23 — Her Majesty Raja Zarith Sofiah, Queen of Malaysia, has expressed concern over the worsening mental health issues among children and adolescents, which have led to loss of life. This effort is specifically aimed at helping teens facing emotional distress, mental health problems and various life challenges. Istana Negara Grand Chamberlain Datuk Azuan Effendy Zairakithnaini led the discussion, which brought together several government agencies, including the Education Ministry, the Women, Family and Community Development Ministry, the Communications Ministry, the Royal Malaysia Police and the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission.

items.title: PTPTN sets RM50 minimum monthly repayment for graduates earning RM2,501 to RM3,000
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 23 — Graduates earning between RM2,501 and RM3,000 a month will only need to repay their National Higher Education Fund Corporation (PTPTN) loans at a minimum rate of RM50 per month, with the flexibility announced in Budget 2027. Deputy Higher Education Minister Adam Adli Abdul Halim said the loan repayment flexibility initiative is expected to benefit more than 400,000 people, helping to ease the financial burden on graduates who have just entered the workforce. He said graduates earning below RM2,500 a month would not need to begin repaying their loans until they reached the stipulated income threshold.

items.title: IGP: Police must treat seniors’ reprimands as lessons, not weakness
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 23 — Inspector-General of Police (IGP) Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail has reminded the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) personnel to maintain discipline and respect for senior officers to preserve the force’s strength and harmony. He said showing regard for senior officers appeared to be declining, raising concerns that this could weaken the police force and undermine its standing among other government departments and agencies. Mohd Khalid said police personnel should respect one another, accept feedback and different opinions, and recognise that they were not always right, adding that they should also remind one another of their responsibilities and respect senior officers to promote cooperation and solidarity within the force.

items.title: RoS challenges court stay on Perikatan deregistration
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 23 — The Registrar of Societies Malaysia (RoS) has filed an appeal against the High Court’s decision allowing Perikatan Nasional (PN) to suspend action by RoS to deregister the political coalition. Judge Azizan also allowed PN’s application to stay the implementation of RoS’ notice suspending all activities of the political coalition pending the court’s decision on its application for judicial review. On Oct 13, the court dismissed PN’s application for an interim stay of the RoS suspension notice but granted the political coalition leave to initiate judicial review proceedings.

items.title: Melaka polls: Perikatan seat talks with Umno to be finalised within days, says Tuan Ibrahim
items.summary: KOTA BHARU, Oct 23 — Perikatan Nasional (PN) is still negotiating to finalise seat allocations for the Melaka state election, with the coalition seeking one or two more seats on top of the seven discussed with Umno so far. PN deputy chairman Datuk Seri Tuan Ibrahim Tuan Man said talks were ongoing, and a final decision, including on any additional seats, was expected soon. Although the seven seats mentioned by Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi are seats not won by Barisan Nasional (BN), we are still negotiating for one or two more seats.

items.title: Malaysia keeps Indonesia firefighting aid offer open, no local companies linked to forest fires
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 23 — Malaysia’s offer to help Indonesia tackle forest fires causing transboundary haze remains open, with the government ready to provide firefighting assets if needed, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said today. Malaysia remains ready to provide assistance and assets if required,” he told his weekly post-Cabinet press conference here. Fahmi said the Prime Minister had expressed appreciation for the strong diplomatic ties between Malaysia and Indonesia and reaffirmed Malaysia’s willingness to assist in efforts to put out the fires.

items.title: Plan your commute: Severe weather warning for KL, Selangor, and nine other states this evening
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 23 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a thunderstorm, heavy rain and strong winds warning for several areas in 11 states and three federal territories until 6 pm today. In Kedah, the affected areas are Bandar Baharu, Kubang Pasu, Padang Terap, Pokok Sena, Pendang, Sik, Kuala Muda, Langkawi, Kulim and Baling, while in Perak, they are Kerian, Selama, Larut Matang, Hulu Perak, Kuala Kangsar, Kinta, Kampar, Batang Padang and Muallim. In Kelantan, the warning covers Gua Musang, Kuala Krai, Jeli, Tanah Merah, Machang and Pasir Puteh, while in Pahang, it covers Pekan, Kuantan, Cameron Highlands, Raub, Bentong, Lipis, Jerantut, Temerloh and Maran.

items.title: Corporate mafia task force’s terms of reference to go before Cabinet next week, says Fahmi
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 23 — The terms of reference for a special task force investigating allegations of a “corporate mafia” will be presented to the Cabinet next week, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said today. He said the task force’s findings would be made public within three months of the completion of the investigation, in line with Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s announcement in Parliament earlier this week. “The Prime Minister also informed the Cabinet that the terms of reference for the special task force that will investigate the findings related to the corporate mafia issue will be presented at next week’s Cabinet meeting,” Fahmi said at his weekly post-Cabinet press conference here.

items.title: UK-based Malaysian lawyer named Multilaw chair-elect
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 23 — Malaysian lawyer Joanne Vengadesan has made history after being elected chair of Multilaw, a global network of law firms spanning over 100 countries with 300 offices. The United Kingdom-based practitioner, who has 25 years of legal experience, was elected at Multilaw’s Global Conference in Prague earlier this month. Joanne said her international upbringing played a significant role in fostering her interest in being part of a global legal community such as Multilaw.

items.title: Fahmi says Malaysians can use any navigation app except Waze, including overseas alternatives
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 23 — Malaysians are free to use any navigation application other than Waze, including alternatives developed locally or overseas, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said today. He said the government was not directing the public towards a single alternative amid concerns over Waze’s data security and ongoing efforts to improve the locally developed TuJu application. People can use various alternative navigation applications other than Waze,” he added.

items.title: BDS Malaysia backs civil service Waze ban, urges public boycott of navigation app
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 23 — BDS Malaysia has welcomed the government’s directive banning civil servants from using Waze and its call for members of the public to stop using the navigation application. In a statement today, the organisation said it supported the directive, citing concerns that the use of Waze could compromise Malaysia’s national security and sovereignty. BDS Malaysia also urged the government to remain consistent in addressing national security concerns.

items.title: Architect charged with molesting senior cop’s son at Melawati gym sauna
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 23 — An architect pleaded not guilty in the Ampang Magistrate’s Court today to a charge of molesting the son of a senior police officer at a gymnasium in Taman Melawati last Sunday. Datuk Saiful Anuar Abdul Aziz, 61, is accused of using criminal force against the 18-year-old victim with intent to outrage his modesty in a sauna room at a gymnasium in a shopping mall in Taman Melawati at 7.10 pm on Oct 18. Magistrate Siti Nur Ain Ariffin granted the accused bail of RM9,000 with one surety, imposed the additional conditions sought by the prosecution and fixed Nov 26 for mention.

items.title: Abang Johari calls for Sarawak state assembly dissolution on Monday
items.summary: KUCHING, Oct 23 — The Sarawak State Legislative Assembly is set to be dissolved on Monday, Oct 26, 2026, paving the way for the 13th state election. Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Tun Openg announced the dissolution at a special press conference at the Satria Pertiwi Complex here this afternoon. He said the decision was made after obtaining the consent of Sarawak Governor Tun Dr Wan Junaidi Tuanku Jaafar.

items.title: Anwar says nationwide Waze ban needs careful study first
items.summary: AMPANG, Oct 23 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said today proposals for a nationwide ban on navigation app Waze required careful study, but did not rule out the possibility if capable local alternatives were available. “It must be studied what are the alternatives first, and if we find that local capabilities are good enough then we may consider prohibiting Waze altogether,” he told reporters after performing Friday prayers here. “Then a check showed Waze is governed only by Israeli laws.
